issues.text: Carried over from r1, now logged in DECISIONS.md section 3 (pending owner): claim 1 rests on The Twelve-Factor App, which has no entry in content/versions.yaml and no refs/ mirror. Not blocking.
issues.quote: The **twelve-factor app** is a list of practices for building apps that are deployed often and to many places.
issues.fix: Owner decision: add a twelve-factor docs root to content/versions.yaml (or a refs/ mirror) and set version_key on claim 1; no lesson edit needed.

issues.text: Round 2: the correction no longer leans on build-once, good. But it only refutes the first half ('the whole of twelve-factor'). Its second half, 'the other eleven are about something else entirely unrelated', is then confirmed: the others 'cover other parts', and a later problem 'has nothing to do with config'. I end up thinking half the misconception is true.
issues.quote: You notice this in later modules, when a problem that has nothing to do with config turns out to be what another factor is about.
issues.fix: Add one clause to the correction saying the others are not unrelated: like Config, they serve the aim in Core concepts, an app that runs reliably in many environments.

issues.text: Section 5 opens with 'The lab passes the factor's quick check', and three sentences later a password is 'visible in the repository'. The quick check asked whether the code could be public without giving away a password. I paused; the link is only implied by 'it protects only a local lab'.
issues.quote: The fake password that ends up in `.env` is written out in `scripts/dev-secrets.sh`, which is committed, so it is visible in the repository.
issues.fix: Extend 'That is deliberate: it protects only a local lab' with ', so publishing the code would give away nothing that protects a real system'.

issues.text: Step 3 now explains Host= and names the three projects. But section 5 said the connection string arrives from `docker-compose.yml`, so I expect it contains Host= too and wonder why it is left out of the search.
issues.quote: which searches the API's three projects for `Host=`, the part of a connection string that names the database server.
issues.fix: Add: 'not `docker-compose.yml`, which is the environment the lab provides, not the API's code'.

issues.text: Carried from round 1, unchanged: sections 2 and 4 and q3 say 'restarting', section 5 and q5's explanation say Compose 'recreated' the container. I still cannot tell whether restarting and recreating are the same thing here.
issues.quote: Moving the API to another database means changing a variable and restarting, not editing code and building again
issues.fix: Add once in section 5: 'recreating the container from the same image is how the API restarts with new variables'.

issues.text: I had to read this sentence twice: the list of three values sits between commas inside another list, so I lost where the subject ended.
issues.quote: the three values that differ, the connection string, the signing key and the environment's name (`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`), arrive from `docker-compose.yml`.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: '... same everywhere. Three values differ and arrive from `docker-compose.yml`: the connection string, the signing key and the environment's name (`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`).'

issues.text: q2: correct option c is close to verbatim from section 6 ('practices to adopt one at a time, as the app needs them. The lab follows Config fully today'), so I can match it by wording.
issues.quote: False, because factors are adopted as the app needs them, and the lab fully follows Config.
issues.fix: Reword c, e.g. 'False: one factor already brings its benefit on its own, and the lab applies Config completely.'
